name: Alex Nuttall
background: Mayor since 2022 (elected with 42.7%). Ward 10 councillor from 2006. Conservative MP for Barrie-Springwater-Oro-Medonte from 2015.
other_priorities: Waterfront performing arts centre; South Barrie YMCA and recreation centre; resident-only summer parking at Centennial Beach.

name: Kay Sayer
background: Moved to Barrie in May 2026. Says she worked for the OPP and RCMP and has experienced homelessness. No prior ballot in Barrie.
other_priorities: Names ending daylight saving time as her top issue, followed by free speech and faith-based community support. Proposes community-owned fibre and micro-grids on arenas.
facebook: Kathleen Paterson (listed by the city; ownership not confirmed)

name: Russell J. Tighe
background: Lifelong Barrie resident with experience in hospitality management, retail and coordinating community services. No prior political career. Has spoken publicly about being in recovery from addiction.
facebook: Russell Tighe Barrie's Next City Mayor

name: Tanya Saari
background: 21-year Barrie resident with a background in finance, real estate, housing and community services. Ran for Ward 3 in 2018 and 2020 and as the federal Liberal candidate in 2021, without winning.
other_priorities: Smoother roads, better snow clearing, safe sidewalks and well-maintained parks.

name: Gary Harvey
background: Retired police officer (35 years). Ward 7 councillor since 2018 (46.9% in 2018; acclaimed in 2022). Chairs the Finance and Responsible Governance Committee. Part-time member of Ontario's Licence Appeal Tribunal.
other_priorities: Splash pad and pickleball and basketball courts at Peggy Hill Community Centre (2027); Holly library branch; Essa Road widening with sidewalks (2028).

name: Michael Lewis
background: Barrie resident since 1980; graduated from Eastview in 1985 and worked at several Barrie employers. Retired, and in his fourth year of a counselling and psychology degree at Georgian College. No party affiliation. Says he has no formal election platform and is running to give Ward 7 residents a voice at city hall.
other_priorities: Parking shortages, which he links to overcrowded single-family homes; lack of municipal services for the property taxes paid.

name: Stefano Agostino
background: First run for Barrie council; no earlier Barrie ballot appearances on record since 2003.
other_priorities: Safety in neighbourhoods and downtown; the future of the 460 hectares of annexed land; road capacity for new development.

name: Shaughna Ainsworth
background: Ran in Ward 1 in 2018 (26.0%, not elected).
other_priorities: Traffic calming on high-speed residential streets; lighting and security; local road repairs; the North Shore Trail, Johnson's Beach and neighbourhood parks.

name: Brent Bowser
background: First run for Barrie council; no earlier Barrie ballot appearances on record since 2003.
other_priorities: Traffic flow and signal timing at the busiest Ward 1 intersections; school-zone safety; parks and green spaces; infrastructure maintenance.

name: Christian Cadera
background: First run for Barrie council; no earlier Barrie ballot appearances on record since 2003. Has spent several years travelling and cites Japan's self-contained communities as a model.
other_priorities: Opposes data centres.

name: Hafiz Rahman
background: His family has been part of the Barrie community for almost 37 years. Has volunteered for almost five years with the Canada Revenue Agency's community tax clinic program, helping seniors, low-income families, newcomers and people experiencing homelessness file returns. Serves on the Lakehead University students' union board and the Georgian College alumni executive council (2026-27). Works at a local bagel shop while studying. Ran in Ward 4 in 2022 (2.2%, not elected).
other_priorities: Sidewalk repairs and community safety; a leash-free dog park.

name: Pauline Stevenson
background: Grew up in Barrie and raised her family here. Has degrees in political science and public relations and worked at the City of Mississauga under Mayor Hazel McCallion. Citizen member of the Heritage Barrie Advisory Committee since 2023. First run for Barrie council; no earlier Barrie ballot appearances on record since 2003.
other_priorities: Absentee landlords and neighbourhood upkeep; speeding on residential streets; student housing issues, working with Georgian College.

name: Frank Casera
background: Moved to Barrie's historic district with his family in 2020. Founded ONE Unltd., a firm that helps leaders and organizations through change, in 2011. First run for Barrie council; no earlier Barrie ballot appearances on record since 2003.
other_priorities: Campaign built on three values: dignity, pride and prosperity. Pledges to protect what's working, act where things aren't, and build for what comes next.

name: Shanicka Edwards
background: Lives in downtown Barrie. Describes herself as a mother, business owner, coach and mentor. Member of the Ontario Trillium Foundation's Simcoe-York grant review team (provincial appointment, 2024-2027) and says she has helped allocate more than $50 million to local charities and non-profits in that role. Ran in Ward 2 in 2022 (27.3%, not elected).
other_priorities: A safe, clean and economically strong downtown, with renewed facade and streetscape incentives and more opportunities for youth; making sure growth works for current residents; maintaining the oldest streets. Supports a new downtown stadium, with planning for parking, traffic and noise.

name: Craig Nixon
background: Moved to Barrie in 1980; spent 30 years in the transportation industry as a manager and owner of a large regional trucking company. Ward 2 councillor since 2022 (37.1%), under the previous ward boundaries. Has led council's Affordability Committee; council appointee to the Downtown Barrie BIA board and the MacLaren Art Centre.
other_priorities: Downtown projects including the Barrie stadium, the performing arts centre, post-secondary campuses and festivals; protecting the waterfront and neighbourhood character as Ward 2 grows.

name: Ajmal Noushahi
background: Ran in Ward 4 in 2022 (6.8%) and for Simcoe County District School Board trustee in 2018 (7.7%), not elected either time.
other_priorities: Downtown safety; fixing streets that have never been repaired and adding traffic signals. Sees the new stadium as a possible economic driver but asks how traffic, parking and noise would be managed.

name: Tracy Strohm
background: Barrie resident since 1967; lives downtown. Retired elementary principal with the Simcoe County District School Board after 37 years; has run a small business and now develops curriculum on contract. Served on the committee that built the Allandale Recreation Centre and co-chaired the city's recreation advisory committee. Ran in Ward 2 in 2022 (13.1%, not elected). Says she is funding her campaign herself.
other_priorities: Revitalizing downtown and nearby neighbourhoods; downtown as a "food desert" without nearby groceries; redeveloping the former Barrie Central site; aging sewer and storm-sewer capacity.

name: Amy Courser
background: Born and raised in Barrie. Spent more than 20 years in digital marketing, ran a small business, and worked in non-profits, manufacturing and construction. Co-founded the non-partisan group Politics for Women and helped raise more than 300,000 pounds of food for the Barrie Food Bank. Ward 4 councillor since 2022 (37.3%), under the previous ward boundaries; now running in Ward 3. Council appointee to the Barrie Public Library Board and the Lake Simcoe Region Conservation Authority board; has chaired the Arts Advisory Committee.
other_priorities: Investing in public services and the library; safer, walkable neighbourhoods.

name: Ben Hughes
background: Grew up in Midhurst and moved to Barrie in 2018; played in the Barrie Minor Hockey Association and then junior hockey. Works as an electrician in Barrie. First run for Barrie council; no earlier Barrie council ballot appearances on record since 2003.
other_priorities: Snow clearing on sidewalks, at bus stops and for transit access as well as on roads.

name: Bryan Jones
background: About 28 years of legal experience, including the last eight as a prosecutor in the Ontario Court of Justice. His family's history in Barrie goes back 150 years; he returned after living in Pickering. First run for office in Barrie; no earlier Barrie ballot appearances on record since 2003.
other_priorities: Traffic safety around schools, including red-light cameras near schools.

name: Ryan Rijo
background: Homeowner and former professional baseball player with the Barrie Baycats. Ran in Ward 3 in 2022 (15.4%, not elected).
other_priorities: The annexed lands from Springwater and Oro-Medonte: development that respects existing residents, farms and rural communities, with residents involved early. Snow clearing and stormwater systems.

name: Iradat Ahmad
background: Ran a road-safety and driver-training business. First run for Barrie council; no earlier Barrie ballot appearances on record since 2003. Says he would be a full-time councillor.
other_priorities: Windrow clearing for every household after snowplows; speeding on residential streets, especially Hurst Drive; police visibility that matches south Barrie's growth.

name: Matthew Corbett
background: First run for office in Barrie; no earlier Barrie ballot appearances on record since 2003.
other_priorities: Says residents raise community safety, traffic and congestion, and responsible growth; wants to bring residents, businesses, community groups and city staff together to solve problems.

name: Lori Galeazza
background: First run for Barrie council; no earlier Barrie ballot appearances on record since 2003. Says she would be a full-time councillor.
other_priorities: Year-round, 24-hour lower speed limits on main roads; better snow removal; protecting the waterfront and parks.
facebook: Elect Lori Galeazza to City of Barrie Ward 4 2026

name: Patrick Harriott-Stewart
background: First run for office in Barrie; no earlier Barrie ballot appearances on record since 2003.
other_priorities: Speeding and community safety, which he calls paramount in the ward.

name: Arif Khan
background: Former Ward 8 councillor, first elected in a 2012 by-election and re-elected in 2014. Provincial appointee to the Barrie Police Service Board, reappointed in 2025.
other_priorities: Building roads for capacity before people move in; calls the delay in widening Mapleview Drive a miscalculation.

name: Duarte Da Silva
background: First-generation Canadian. Studied radio broadcasting at Humber Polytechnic and professional communication at Royal Roads University. Has worked in business development and manufacturing, and most recently as a constituency assistant in a member of Parliament's office; now does communications consulting. First run for Barrie council; no earlier Barrie ballot appearances on record since 2003.
other_priorities: Real consultation on annexation; closing the gap in infrastructure investment between north and south Ward 5; development at 49 Miller Drive (611 homes with two entrances on one street); safety on County Road 90.
facebook: Vote Duarte Da Silva for Barrie Ward 5

name: Robert Thomson
background: Ward 5 councillor since 2018 (55.2% in 2018; acclaimed in 2022) and Deputy Mayor since 2022. Vice-chair of the Barrie Police Service Board; council appointee to the Simcoe County Housing Corporation board.
other_priorities: Traffic calming, permanent speed humps and infill sidewalks such as Edgehill Drive; finishing the performing arts centre and the northwest library.

name: Nasar George Nader
background: Ward 6 resident since 2022. Part-time educational assistant with the Simcoe County District School Board, with 25 years in customer service and hospitality and 25 years of volunteering. Came to Canada as a refugee and says he and his family were once homeless for a few months. First run for office in Barrie; no earlier Barrie ballot appearances on record since 2003.
other_priorities: Bringing residents together; says residents raise crime, mental health, homelessness and speeding.

name: Nigussie Nigussie
background: Came to Canada in 2008 as a political refugee from Ethiopia, first settling in Regina, Sask.; earlier worked as a freelance journalist and author. Public servant, social worker and community development professional. Ward 6 councillor since 2022 (30.0%), under the previous ward boundaries. Chairs the Seniors and Accessibility Advisory Committee; council appointee to the Barrie Public Library Board and the Simcoe Muskoka District Health Unit Board of Health.
other_priorities: A new crosswalk at Mapleton Avenue and Batteaux Street; flood mitigation near the Bear Creek Wetlands and Marta Crescent; the $5.6 million Tiffin Street reconstruction; protecting the Ardagh Bluffs and Beacon Glen trails; an annual resident outreach program.

name: Christel Pena
background: Longtime Barrie resident and parent. First run for office in Barrie; no earlier Barrie ballot appearances on record since 2003.
other_priorities: School transportation and school-zone traffic safety; transit; support for local businesses.

name: Samina Alim
background: Career in law, public policy and judicial work. First run for office in Barrie; no earlier Barrie ballot appearances on record since 2003.
other_priorities: Coordinated action on homelessness and addiction; more pedestrian crossings and traffic calming; protecting natural, agricultural and recreational spaces.

name: Amanda Fellows
background: Works in community mental health. Ran for Simcoe Muskoka Catholic District School Board trustee in 2022 (37.8%, not elected).
other_priorities: Monthly Ward 8 town halls; planning ahead for traffic pressure points and more proactive traffic calming.

name: Jim Harris
background: Ward 8 councillor since 2018 (30.8% in 2018; 79.0% in 2022), under the previous ward boundaries. Co-chair of the Affordability Committee; has chaired the Performing Arts Centre task force.
other_priorities: Integrating the Allandale transit hub into the area; Ward 8 as the first area to pilot speed cameras; traffic calming in school zones.

name: Norm Costello
background: Described by Frequency News as a former New Blue Party official. Ran in Ward 9 in 2022 (13.9%, not elected).
other_priorities: Communication between residents and the Ward 9 councillor; road and utility upgrades in the Hewitt's secondary plan area before congestion builds; better snow removal with windrow plows.

name: Sergio Morales
background: Ward 9 councillor since 2014 (51.6% in 2014; acclaimed in 2018; 67.8% in 2022), under the previous ward boundaries. Chairs the Community Safety Committee; has chaired the Finance and Corporate Services Committee.
other_priorities: The overdue Ward 9 recreation centre and library at Huronia Road and McKay Road East; opening the Allandale train station; cutting red tape for a discount grocery store in Ward 9.

name: Asmar Naveed
background: First run for office in Barrie; no earlier Barrie ballot appearances on record since 2003. His campaign website says he has stepped back from active campaigning; his name remains on the ballot.
other_priorities: A shared multi-use path on one side of Dean Avenue; a snow-plow tracker that shows whether a street has actually been plowed; a southeast community and recreation centre.

name: Dave Weingarten
background: Local videographer and Ward 9 resident; says he is not affiliated with any political party. First run for office in Barrie; no earlier Barrie ballot appearances on record since 2003.
other_priorities: Road maintenance, traffic calming and snow removal as safety issues, especially for seniors.

name: William Cadeau
background: Barrie resident for more than 10 years. Canadian military veteran who served as Army medical staff at several base hospitals and unit medical stations; now works locally in Barrie. First run for office in Barrie; no earlier Barrie ballot appearances on record since 2003.
other_priorities: Improving roads and public services; supporting local businesses; safe and clean neighbourhoods.

name: Bryn Hamilton
background: Ward 10 councillor since 2022 (52.3%), under the previous ward boundaries. Chairs the Infrastructure and Community Investment Committee; member of the Executive Committee.
other_priorities: Speeding, cut-through traffic and difficult intersections; reducing the impact of the Mapleview Drive closure; more snow-removal funding for the hardest-hit neighbourhoods; the South Barrie Recreation Centre and Library.

name: Georgy Kapustin
background: First run for office in Barrie; no earlier Barrie ballot appearances on record since 2003.
other_priorities: A second exit at Barrie South GO Station; added turn lanes at major intersections; designated employment areas so Barrie isn't a bedroom community for Toronto.
